about: The geometry kernel's golden store (chapter 28.13): every golden digest, SHA-256 in lowercase hexadecimal, keyed by kernel edition, golden id and operation versions. Read by geom_test::golden (store.rs explains every field and rule). Never edit a digest without appending a history record holding the old digest, its kind (bug, improvement or corpus), the piece and why; a kernel owner approves every edit to an existing golden (.github/workflows/kernel-golden.yml checks it), and nothing in a frozen edition ever changes. Run `cargo run -p geom-test --bin golden -- check` after any change.

goldens.what: geom-num's determinism corpus: 88,218 calls into every module of the numbers layer (predicates, planes, three-plane points, grid steps, wide integers, error-free transformations, intervals, the maths module and the scalars), each result in the canonical encoding of tests/determinism.rs.

history.why: The correctly rounded maths of piece G05 (issue #174): 92 of G02's 7,677 maths records moved by one unit in the last place to the correctly rounded value (exp 9, ln 3, sinpi 52, cospi 19, atan2 9); the refusals of Interval::exp and Interval::ln moved from the interval section to the maths section, now certified; 2,700 records were added from their own generator (SEED_G05) for the libm twins and the interval versions. No error changed; the other sections give G02's digests unchanged.

Interval::atan2 is certified now (piece G47): its refusal (index 2) left the interval section, and the maths section gains 601 records of it (index 32) from a generator of their own (SEED_G47), after every earlier record; no other record moved, and the sections predicates, planes, tpi, grid, wide, eft and scalars are unchanged. The same digest on wasm32 under Wasmtime, where exp's exact product error is now Dekker's two-product.

goldens.what: The draw corpus of geom_num::rng (Philox4x32-10, piece G32): at least 20,000 draws of every kind over six seeds and streams from six starting positions, in the canonical encoding of tests/rng_determinism.rs.
The stream-range corpus of geom_num::rng (piece G32): stream ranges of every size and index, their streams and their errors, in the canonical encoding of tests/rng_determinism.rs.

Double-double arithmetic and ExactSum (piece G25) on 6,000 adversarial operand pairs at every exponent: every DD operation, two_prod_fma and fma, 903,792 recorded bytes in the encoding of tests/attack_g25.rs.

The five correctly rounded maths functions of piece G05 (sinpi, cospi, exp, ln and atan2) over 100,000 inputs, each result a word (a value's bits or a marker for its error) as tests/attack_g05.rs records it; the SHA-256 of the bytes whose 64-bit FNV-1a digest G05 pinned.

The input-shuffle hook on geom-num's order-free contracts (piece G19): ExactSum over seeded term sets added in their own order and in shuffled orders, one by one, as slices, as streams and as shuffled chunks merged in shuffled order, and DD addition and multiplication and two_sum in both operand orders, in the encoding of tests/order_free.rs.

geom-math's determinism corpus (piece G03): vectors, floats, double-double, grid, rational, general and typed transforms, boxes, frames and shifts, at least 30,000 calls in the canonical encoding of tests/determinism.rs.

history.why: The correctly rounded sinpi and cospi of piece G05 (CORE-MATH ports in place of an msun-method approximation), which geom-math's rotations call: only the two sections that build rotations from them changed, transform (6773dadd...852b18 before) and boxes (2e8f3297...bc7e3e before); every other section's digest is the same. Recorded on main in G03's pull request (commit bbbc379), before the store existed.

Piece G48 moved geom-math onto geom-num's double-double type (piece G25) and made out-of-range conversions report the exact coordinate. Only two sections changed: dd (a675b95c...61b257 before), which now exercises geom-num's DD, the one geom-math's frames use, with its own algorithms, tighter proven bounds and errors (division by zero NotFinite, the root of a negative OutsideDomain); and frames (ae980551...e555d700 before), whose OutOfRange values are now the exact rounded coordinate, saturated only beyond i128, in the order height, x, y, where G03 reported estimates. Every successful conversion is unchanged: both pieces round correctly, and the rounding is unique. The other eight sections' digests are the same.

goldens.what: geom-math's attack workload (piece G03): map conversions both ways, double-double arithmetic and transform classification and inversion, as tests/attack_g03.rs records it.

history.why: The correctly rounded sinpi and cospi of piece G05 (CORE-MATH ports in place of an msun-method approximation), which the workload's rotations call; sqrt, abs, floor, ceil and round_ties_even, the only other maths functions geom-math calls, are unchanged. Recorded on main in G03's pull request (commit c19cca4), before the store existed.

Piece G48 moved geom-math onto geom-num's double-double type (piece G25): the workload's double-double arithmetic (add, mul, div and sqrt of random operands) now runs geom-num's DD, with its own algorithms and tighter proven bounds, so some results differ in their last bits and its errors differ (division by zero NotFinite, the root of a negative OutsideDomain). The workload's map conversions hash only successful results, which are correctly rounded in both pieces and so unchanged, and its transforms are untouched.

goldens.what: geom-math's frame workload (piece G48): map to frame from doubles and from exact decimal text, frame to map, in metres, feet, Clarke's foot and random linear units, Map and Ground frames with 64-bit scale factors, out-of-range values, decimal text forms, units from decimals and exact shifts, as tests/attack_g48.rs records it.

geom-run's parallel helpers (piece G04) on the serial executor and on pools of 1, 2, 3 and 8 threads with chunk sizes 1, 7 and 4,096: every answer, error and meter, in the canonical encoding of tests/golden.rs.
3,000 draws of geom-test's grid sampler (piece G11) from the default seed, every coordinate's little-endian bytes; the SHA-256 of the bytes whose 64-bit FNV-1a digest G11 pinned.
The first proptest case of seeds 0 to 63 from geom-test's grid strategies (piece G11), every coordinate's little-endian bytes; the SHA-256 of the bytes whose 64-bit FNV-1a digest G11 pinned.
The permutations of 0 to 63 inputs the input-shuffle hook draws from the default seed (piece G19), every index as eight little-endian bytes: the orders every order-free golden runs in.

geom-bench's golden file (piece G06, chapter 23.13's output hashes): the SHA-256 of every benchmark's inputs and results, one line per benchmark, which every benchmark harness checks; pinned here by the SHA-256 of the file's text with LF line ends, so an edit to it is an edit to the store.

history.why: 74 new benchmarks: the line-plane point, the 2D crossing and their generated predicates; no existing digest moved
8 new benchmarks: the perturbed predicates' exact path and ties; no existing digest moved

176 new benchmarks: the plain-i128 and width-aware limb variants of every generated exact path, Avnaim et al.'s signs of orient2d and orient3d, and Wide32 at the widths Wide is measured at; no existing digest moved; merged after G30's 8 perturbation benchmarks, whose rows are kept unchanged.
2 new benchmarks: Interval::atan2 on typical and extreme boxes, now that its enclosure is built; no existing digest moved

12 new benchmarks in two new groups: newton (Krawczyk and Hansen-Sengupta steps on a circle and a line, and on a system of four unknowns) and dual (Jacobians over reals and over intervals), each on typical and extreme inputs; no existing digest moved

6 new benchmarks in two new groups: isolate (the root-isolation engine on a cubic in one unknown and on a circle and a line) and ball (a cubic evaluated in double-double balls), each on typical and extreme inputs; no existing digest moved

ExactSum's Debug text, by which canonical.rs encodes a sum, now writes the sum's value only (its digits after a carry propagation, its special values and its lost flag, and `..` for the rest), not the raw chunks and the additions left before a propagation (chapter 28.8; Gate 1's ledger review): the 12 exact_sum digests moved, the results of add, add_slice and add_iter, the inputs of round and round_ieee, and both of merge; no result changed, and every other benchmark's digests are the same; merged after G53's 6 isolate and ball benchmarks, whose rows are kept unchanged

26 new count benchmarks on the hot paths of phase 2's code pieces (decision 32.44): geom-math 7, geom-curve 5, geom-surface 5, geom-nurbs 3, geom-linalg 2, geom-bvh 2, geom-num 2; no existing digest moved
3 new count benchmarks on geom-intersect's canonical order (decision 32.44): a list of items sorted and proven disjoint, a circle's key, a pair of lines put in order; no existing digest moved

7 new count benchmarks on the exact decisions on lines and quadrics (decision 32.44): a line with a sphere, cylinder, cone and torus, parallel directions, an axis's gap and a tangent sphere; no existing digest moved

5 new count benchmarks on where curves meet (decision 32.44): two segments, two circles, a line with a circle, two cubics and a loop; merged with G159's quadric and G162's projection lines; no existing digest moved
3 new count benchmarks on where curves meet surfaces (decision 32.44): a line through a plane, a line along a torus's equator and a cubic through a graph; no existing digest moved
2 new count benchmarks on geom-intersect's tracer (decision 32.44): a sphere through a plane patch and a torus's silhouette; no existing digest moved
1 new count benchmark on geom-intersect's subdivision (decision 32.44): a sphere through a plane patch; no existing digest moved
1 new count benchmark on geom-intersect's marching (decision 32.44): the branches of a sphere through a plane patch; no existing digest moved

1 new count benchmark on geom-intersect's contact analysis (decision 32.44): a sphere resting on a plane patch. march_plate's digest moves with it: the march now pads each parameter's box at that parameter's speed, without which it could not walk a NURBS surface against a plane at grid scale.

1 new count benchmark on geom-intersect's poles and seams (decision 32.44): a whole sphere through a plane holding both its poles, one loop joined through each. trace_patch's, march_plate's and trace_silhouette's digests move with it: their results' branches now say where they pass a seam, a knot line or a pole (Branch::passes, 12.10), which their Debug text writes, empty here.

goldens.what: geom-nurbs's knot operations (piece G56) on a fixed corpus of 96 curves of degrees 1 to 5, 7, 9 and 12 and 24 surfaces: insertion, refinement (by new knots, by the curve's own and by both), elevation, Bezier extraction, knot removal and degree reduction at several tolerances, and derivative curves and surfaces, each result's knots, control points, weights and deviation, in the encoding of tests/operations_determinism.rs.

The fitting operations of geom-nurbs at FitVersion::V1 (piece G58): 64 curve interpolations, 16 with end derivatives, 32 least-squares curves, 16 weighted least-squares curves with point and derivative constraints, 8 surface interpolations, 8 least-squares surfaces, 8 approximations to a stated error (a helix, a corner and noisy data, single and multiple knots) and 5 refusals: 157 results in the canonical encoding of tests/fit_determinism.rs.

The Bernstein toolkit of geom-nurbs (piece G59): 200 surfaces (degrees 1 to 3, one to three spans each way, rational half the time) with every patch's interval coefficients, box, derivative boxes, fat plane and normal patch; 200 pairs of plane curves with every piece's box, derivative box, fat line and clips; 50 scalar, dot and cross products; 20 exact normal patches and plane coefficients of grid patches; and 4 refusals: 5960 results in the canonical encoding of tests/bernstein_determinism.rs.

The analytic curve kinds of geom-curve (piece G61): 40 rounds of a line, circle, ellipse, hyperbola, parabola, polynomial and involute in 2D and the same with a helix in 3D, each evaluated in doubles and enclosed at five parameters, bounded with three derivative bounds over a span, converted to NURBS (knots, control points, weights, parameter map and deviation), split, reversed and transformed (each evaluated, with its deviation); and 6 refusals: 30606 results in the canonical encoding of tests/analytic_determinism.rs.

history.why: The analytic kinds' bounds and derivative bounds are their closed-form extents now (piece G67): each coordinate's range over the span from its values at the span's ends and at its critical points in closed form, where G61 took the interval extension over eighths of a turn. So the bound records of the line, circle, ellipse, hyperbola, parabola, helix and involute moved inward, and so did the deviations of the helix's and involute's NURBS forms, whose Taylor remainders rest on derivative bounds. The change is in the bound route alone (form.rs's bound and derivative_bound); the result count (30606) and the refusals (6) are unchanged.

A grid transform that moves a circle's centre exactly now states deviation 0 (chapter 7: grid transforms stay exact; piece G69's law catalogue found circles on frames with irrational unit vectors stating about 1e-14, from comparing interval enclosures that are never points). The corpus's quarter turns of circles moved; the kinds, their data and every other record are unchanged, and so are the result count (30606) and the refusals (6).

goldens.what: The bulge polyline, trimmed, composite, offset and curve-on-surface kinds of geom-curve (piece G62): 30 rounds of a bulge polyline (straight segments, semicircles and major arcs, widths half the time), a trimmed NURBS curve, a composite of a line, an arc and a NURBS curve, three offsets (of a circle in 2D, of a helix against a reference direction, of a helix by distances) and a curve on a surface, each evaluated in doubles and enclosed at five parameters, bounded with two derivative bounds over a span, converted to NURBS (knots, control points, weights, parameter map and deviation), split, reversed and transformed (each evaluated, with its deviation); and 6 refusals: 10506 results in the canonical encoding of tests/compound_determinism.rs.

history.why: The analytic kinds' bounds and derivative bounds are their closed-form extents now (piece G67). The bulge, trimmed, composite and offset kinds bound their analytic leaves through them, a composite's enclosures over a parameter interval use them, and the offsets' NURBS caches take their Taylor remainders from them, so those records moved. No compound kind's own code changed; the result count (10506) and the refusals (6) are unchanged.

A grid transform that moves a bulge polyline's vertices, or a circle's centre, exactly now states deviation 0 (chapter 7; piece G69's law catalogue), and so do the trimmed and composite curves built on them. The corpus's quarter turns of those curves moved; the result count (10506) and the refusals (6) are unchanged.

goldens.what: The transition kind of geom-curve (piece G63): 30 rounds of one transition per curvature law (clothoid, Helmert, Bloss, cosine, sine, cant-coupled, and IFC's polynomial, cosine and sine spirals), each with its panel count and remainder and, at six stations, its point and three derivatives in doubles, its enclosures to the third derivative, its turn and its curvature; and 6 refusals (the five asked for, and one random polynomial spiral past the panel cap): 6731 results in the canonical encoding of tests/transition_determinism.rs.

The transition kind's operations in geom-curve (piece G64): 6 rounds of one transition per curvature law (clothoid, Helmert, Bloss, cosine, sine, cant-coupled, and IFC's polynomial, cosine and sine spirals), each with its NURBS form (every knot, control point and the deviation), its split at 0.37 of its length (both parts' domains and enclosures there), its reversal, a reversed part with its bound, its bound and three derivative bounds over a span, and its images under a certified rotation and a uniform scale of the plane (kind, deviation and an enclosure); and 6 refusals: 978 results in the canonical encoding of tests/transition_ops_determinism.rs.

history.why: Piece G67 gives a transition's bound and derivative bounds by pieces over which the heading turns at most a sixteenth of a half-turn, each boxed from the certified points at both its ends (G64 boxed each panel from its start alone, and bounded a derivative by one interval evaluation over the span). So the bound records moved inward, and so did the NURBS forms' deviations, whose Taylor remainders rest on the derivative bounds. The result count (978) and the refusals (6) are unchanged.

goldens.what: The analytic and swept surface kinds of geom-surface (piece G65): 12 rounds of a plane, cylinder, cone, sphere and torus on random frames and a surface of revolution, an extrusion and a ruled surface on fixed profiles, each enclosed at nine parameter pairs, bounded with both derivative bounds and the normal bound over a box, converted to NURBS (knots, net, weights, both parameter maps and deviation), split and reversed in each direction and transformed (each enclosed, with its deviation); and 5 refusals: 2693 results in the canonical encoding of tests/surface_determinism.rs.

history.why: The analytic surface kinds' bounds, derivative bounds and partials over a box are their closed-form extents now (piece G67): a plane's, cylinder's and cone's (and their affine images') by separating the parameters, a sphere's by its factored form, a torus's by c + (R + r·cos πv)·G(u) + Q(v), where G65 took the interval extension over eighths of a turn. The change is in that route alone (a region of one point keeps the terms' own enclosure, and normal bounds are unchanged); the result count (2693) and the refusals (5) are unchanged.

A grid transform that moves a cylinder's, cone's, sphere's or torus's centre exactly now states deviation 0 (chapter 7; piece G69's law catalogue found about 1e-15 stated, from comparing interval enclosures of irrational unit vectors). The corpus's quarter turns of those kinds moved; its revolutions turn about the origin, so piece G69's fix of a revolution's placement moved none of them; the result count (2693) and the refusals (5) are unchanged.

goldens.what: The offset surface kind of geom-surface (piece G66): 3 rounds of offsets of a bicubic NURBS patch with an interior knot each way (rational in the second round), of a cylinder and of a torus on random frames, and in the first an offset of an offset, each enclosed at nine parameter pairs, with its partials to order 3 at three, bounded with both derivative bounds and the normal bound over a box, converted to NURBS by default and the first patch's offset within 1e-1 (knots, net, weights, both parameter maps and deviation), split and reversed in each direction and transformed (each enclosed, with its deviation; the offset of an offset is not converted and moves by a grid mirror); and 4 refusals: 314 results in the canonical encoding of tests/offset_determinism.rs.

history.why: An offset bounds itself and builds its certified cache from its base's bounds and partials over boxes, which for the analytic bases are their closed-form extents now (piece G67): the records that rest on them moved. The offset kind's own code did not change; the result count (314) and the refusals (4) are unchanged.

A rational NURBS patch's partials over a box now start from the hull of its Euclidean control points (chapter 19.3's interval quotient rule, piece G68) rather than from the quotient of the boxes of its numerator and weight. The second round's offset is of a rational patch, and an offset bounds itself and builds its certified cache from its base's partials over boxes, so the records that rest on them moved. The offset kind's own code did not change; the result count (314) and the refusals (4) are unchanged.

A grid mirror of an analytic base now states deviation 0 (piece G69), so a grid mirror of an offset of such a base is an offset again, its distance negated, by the offset kind's own rule (an exact move of the base keeps the kind), where before the base's stated rounding sent it to its moved NURBS cache. The result count (314) and the refusals (4) are unchanged.

goldens.what: Every surface kind's second-derivative and normal-derivative bounds (piece G68): 6 rounds of a rational bicubic NURBS patch with an interior knot each way and weights from 2^-10 to 2^10 (with 1e-3 and 1e3 among them) and a nonrational biquadratic one, each over its whole domain, a quarter of it, a box of a hundredth of each side and a box across its interior knots; and a plane, a cylinder, a cone (at its apex and away from it), a sphere (at its pole and away from it), a torus and an affine image of a torus on random frames, over one box each. For every box the partials to order 2, the second-derivative bound with its chord constant M, and the normal-derivative bound; and 2 refusals: 386 results in the canonical encoding of tests/derivative_determinism.rs.

The box tree of geom-bvh (piece G54): 2D and 3D trees over 22 fixed sets of 1 to 9,000 boxes (sparse, dense, nested and all equal, the largest built with the parallel subtree phase), each tree's canonical bytes, the keys meeting eight query boxes, its pairs and its pairs with another tree both ways, the work each of those walks charged, and one refit of each, 3,970,021 bytes in the encoding of tests/tree_determinism.rs.

The Morton-sorted cell index of geom-bvh (piece G55): indexes over seven fixed sets of 1 to 20,000 grid points (sparse over the frame, dense, clustered at the frame's edge, the eight corners and 300 equal points), each index's canonical bytes, the keys within six radii of twelve centres and the work each search charged, and every pair within two radii, in the encoding of tests/cells_determinism.rs.

Brent's zero and minimum, the generated Gauss-Legendre and Gauss-Kronrod rules and the adaptive integrator (piece G51): every rule's nodes and weights, 1,790 results over fixed problems and every point each search and integration evaluated, in order, in the canonical encoding of tests/roots_quadrature_determinism.rs.

The dual numbers and the interval Newton operators (piece G52): every elemental operation on 300 pairs of dual reals and 300 pairs of dual intervals, with the tripwire's refusals at singular points; the values and Jacobians of two fixed systems at 50 points and over 50 boxes; and the Krawczyk and Hansen-Sengupta operators, up to five steps each from boxes around the zeros of 60 seeded systems in each of one to four unknowns, with singular, empty and failing systems: 10,337 results in the canonical encoding of tests/dual_newton_determinism.rs.

The double-double balls and the root-isolation engine (piece G53): every ball operation on 400 seeded pairs, results and errors alike; and the engine, by both operators, on seeded product systems (24, 12, 6 and 4 in one to four unknowns), on zeros on split lines and on the domain's boundary, zeros closer than the floor, multiple zeros, a dependent system, a zero without a derivative, the double-double fallbacks, and every cap (the work and logical-memory budgets, an unreachable target, an imprecise position, a box that cannot be split): 6,181 results in the canonical encoding of tests/isolate_determinism.rs, with the work and logical memory each isolation charged.

geom-math's rational rotations (piece G46): 2D searches for 175 directions at seven bounds, 3D searches for 129 quaternion targets at five bounds, 300 compositions at three bounds (exact and re-approximated) and as typed transforms, images of grid points at the frame's edges, every result's matrix, inverse, direction, rational and floating-point forms, and typed transforms of every variant composed, as tests/rotation_determinism.rs records them.

The singular value decompositions (one-sided Jacobi and Golub-Kahan) and the symmetric eigensolver of geom-linalg (piece G50): 256 matrices of every shape from 1 x 1 to 8 x 8 (random, integer, graded to 2^-600 and exactly rank-deficient), both SVDs of each and the eigendecomposition of each square one's symmetric part, and two refusals for want of work: 546 results in the canonical encoding of tests/spectral_determinism.rs.

The dense decompositions and solves of geom-linalg (piece G49): 256 matrices of every shape from 1 x 1 to 8 x 8 (random, integer, graded to 2^-600 and exactly rank-deficient), each through the pivoted QR, the complete orthogonal decomposition (rank, least squares, null space) and the canonical null space, each square one also through LU (and a solve), both triangular solves, Cholesky of A^T A + I (and a solve) and of A itself, and the tridiagonal solve, and four refusals for want of work: 1568 results in the canonical encoding of tests/dense_determinism.rs.
